themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 4 complaints THIS WEEK compared to a 0.4-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 967% increase—suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors or enforcement gap in Lower Manhattan.
evidence: 4 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Vendor Enforcement is the #1 complaint category overall (1,211 complaints over 90 days), suggesting systemic issue
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed food vendors operating with impunity in specific Lower Manhattan hotspots?
Has DOH enforcement staffing or frequency changed recently, explaining the sudden spike?

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Complaints Jump
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints tripled to 3 complaints LAST WEEK from a 0.4-complaint weekly average—a 700% spike with z-score 5.42—potentially indicating deteriorating building conditions or increased awareness in older Lower Manhattan structures.
evidence: 3 asbestos complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
1,148 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (980 alterations) suggests active renovation work that may disturb asbestos-containing materials
reporting_angles: Are renovation projects in Lower Manhattan's older building stock inadvertently exposing residents to asbestos?
What are tenants' rights when asbestos is discovered, and are landlords complying with remediation timelines?

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints surged 49 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO compared to a 16.8-complaint weekly average—a 192% increase with z-score 6.02—suggesting either construction activity, new residents, or hospitality-related disruption in Lower Manhattan residential areas.
evidence: 49 residential noise complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 16.8 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Noise-Residential is the 5th-ranked complaint category (287 complaints over 90 days)
980 building alterations filed in last 90 days could be driving construction-related noise
reporting_angles: Are construction projects concentrated in residential neighborhoods without adequate noise control?
Has short-term rental activity (Airbnb, hotels) increased noise complaints in specific blocks or buildings?

themes_detail.label: Paint/Plaster Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Paint and plaster complaints reached 6 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO from a 0.4-complaint weekly average—a 1500% spike with the highest z-score (11.62)—indicating widespread interior deterioration across Lower Manhattan buildings, likely tied to aging infrastructure and deferred maintenance.
evidence: 6 paint/plaster complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
1500% spike with z-score of 11.62 (highest severity rating in dataset)
Community Board budget repeatedly requests elementary school renovations, suggesting broader infrastructure aging concerns
reporting_angles: What percentage of Lower Manhattan residential units have failing paint/plaster, and are landlords meeting HPD compliance deadlines?
Are lead paint hazards present in these deteriorating units, especially in buildings housing families with children?

themes_detail.label: Plumbing System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints jumped to 20 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO from a 4.0-complaint weekly average—a 400% spike with z-score 4.82—compounded by 247 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days, suggesting systemic infrastructure failures in older Lower Manhattan buildings.
evidence: 20 plumbing complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 4.0 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Heat/Hot Water is the 8th-ranked complaint category (247 complaints over 90 days), suggesting interconnected systems issues
980 building alterations filed in last 90 days may indicate landlords addressing deferred maintenance reactively
reporting_angles: Are Lower Manhattan's aging pipes and boiler systems failing simultaneously, and what is the city's remediation timeline?
Which landlords have repeat plumbing violations, and are they facing HPD enforcement?
